D31·0q86 — 2026-09-22 — replaced by D32·45tr
rule: Hot-path Rust never calls a libm transcendental directly; each JavaScript Math function it needs is ported from V8's implementation with that target's contraction, and cross-checked against the runner's own Node on every CI target.
chose: Reproduce Math.log by porting V8's fdlibm __ieee754_log into js_math.rs, with each a*b+c fused on aarch64 and unfused elsewhere, pinned as HOTPATH P10 and proven per CI target against that runner's own Node (tests/js_log_crosscheck.rs)
over: (a) f64::ln, the platform libm; (b) plain fdlibm on every target; (c) masking or rounding scores before comparing
because: D2: JavaScript semantics, never Rust defaults. On darwin-arm64 Node 24.15, f64::ln differed from Math.log in the last bit on 43,532 of 1,048,616 BM25-shaped inputs (4.2%, e.g. ln(8/3)); plain fdlibm still differed on 12,317; fdlibm with the aarch64 fusion matched all of them. An ulp decides the lessons cuts (LESSON_OVER_SHARE 0.5, runner-up 0.6, the corpus floor) and exact-score ties, so the existing fold-path rank_lexical was already off. The x86-64 variant is inferred (no FMA in baseline x86-64) and proves itself on the first CI run
